note: Mercury Editor is a drag-and-drop page builder built on layout_paragraphs + style_options. It replaces the edit form of enabled bundles with an edit screen at /mercury-editor/{entity}. Config lives in one object mercury_editor.settings (route mercury_editor.settings at /admin/config/content/mercury-editor). It has NO permissions of its own (core 'administer site configuration'), no Drush, no plugin types. Real keys: bundles (entity_type->bundle map that enables the editor), edit_screen_theme, mobile_presets (list of {name,width,height}), skip_create_form, dialog_settings, dialog_tray_width (default 400), rollover_padding_block/inline. To avoid disturbing the shared 'article' bundle's edit form, the introspection/execution cases here exercise the safe scalar keys (dialog_tray_width, edit_screen_theme, mobile_presets) rather than toggling bundles. Scripts restore shipped defaults explicitly.

evals.prompt: On Drupal 11 with the mercury_editor module enabled, how do I make a specific content type use the Mercury Editor drag-and-drop editor, where is that stored, and what admin path configures it?
evals.expected_output: Enable the bundle on the settings form at /admin/config/content/mercury-editor (route mercury_editor.settings). It is stored in mercury_editor.settings under bundles.<entity_type>.<bundle> (e.g. bundles.node.landing_page: landing_page). The bundle must be set up for Layout Paragraphs.

evals.prompt: What two contrib modules is Mercury Editor built on / does it require, and what kind of editing experience does it provide?
evals.expected_output: Mercury Editor requires layout_paragraphs and style_options. It provides a full-screen, drag-and-drop page builder with live preview that replaces the standard entity edit form for enabled bundles.

evals.prompt: When a bundle is managed by Mercury Editor, at what URL / route does the drag-and-drop edit screen live, and does the module define any permissions of its own?
evals.expected_output: The edit screen is the mercury_editor.editor route at /mercury-editor/{mercury_editor_entity}. Mercury Editor ships no permissions of its own; access relies on core 'administer site configuration' and the underlying Layout Paragraphs/entity permissions.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Mercury Editor's editing tray width has been customised. Inspect the live configuration and tell me the current tray width (in pixels).
evals.expected_output: mercury_editor.settings dialog_tray_width is 555. Read via drush cget mercury_editor.settings dialog_tray_width.

evals.prompt: Mercury Editor's edit tray on this site has been set to use a specific theme. Inspect the running configuration and state which theme (machine name) is configured for the Mercury Editor edit tray.
evals.expected_output: mercury_editor.settings edit_screen_theme is 'claro'. Read via drush cget mercury_editor.settings edit_screen_theme.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Mercury Editor so that its edit tray is 600 pixels wide and uses the 'claro' theme for the edit tray. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In mercury_editor.settings set dialog_tray_width=600 and edit_screen_theme='claro' (via the settings form at /admin/config/content/mercury-editor or drush/configFactory).

evals.prompt: Add a mobile preview preset to Mercury Editor named exactly 'Tablet ME' that is 800 pixels wide and 1000 pixels tall, keeping it among the module's mobile presets. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In mercury_editor.settings mobile_presets contains an entry {name: 'Tablet ME', width: 800, height: 1000}. On the settings form add the line 'Tablet ME|800|1000' to Mobile presets, or append it to the config list.
